narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the length of the loan you requested, your credit history, and your employment situation. The requested loan term of 48 months was by far the strongest reason for the denial. Most approved applicants ask for about 19 months, so your much longer repayment period strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Your past delays in repaying credit also increased the risk score, though this effect was smaller. Finally, being unemployed worked against you as well, since only 6.8% of approved applicants are unemployed while most have been employed for several years.

Taken together, these three pieces of information led the model to conclude that the overall risk was too high to approve the loan.

You should focus on improving the factors you can change. Consider applying again later for a shorter loan amount after you have secured stable employment and cleared any recent payment delays. This combination would likely improve your chances significantly.
